summary: Tawhid is the foundational principle of Islam: the absolute oneness of Allah in His lordship, worship, and names and attributes. It is the first obligation upon every Muslim and the purpose behind creation.
content:
Tawhid — declaring and affirming the absolute oneness of Allah — is the cornerstone of the Islamic creed and the purpose for which creation was made. Allah says in the Quran: 'I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me' (51:56). The entire message of every prophet, from Adam to Muhammad (peace be upon them all), was a call to tawhid.

Classical scholars of Ahl us-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah have categorised tawhid into three inseparable divisions, each addressing a distinct dimension of Allah's oneness.

## 1. Tawhid al-Rububiyyah — Oneness in Lordship

This category affirms that Allah alone is the Creator, Sustainer, Owner, and Controller of all existence. He alone brings things into being, causes death, sends rain, decrees matters, and manages every affair of the universe. Nothing happens except by His will and decree.

Allah says: 'Say: Who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Or who owns hearing and sight? And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living? And who manages every affair?' (10:31). Even the polytheists of Makkah affirmed this level of tawhid; what they lacked was the next level.

## 2. Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah — Oneness in Worship

This is the most central category and the one the Quran emphasises most. It means that all acts of worship — prayer, fasting, supplication (du'a), sacrifice, vows, love, fear, and hope — must be directed exclusively to Allah. No created being, however righteous, shares in the right to be worshipped.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Du'a is worship' (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi — graded sahih by al-Albani). Directing du'a or any act of worship to other than Allah — whether a prophet, saint, or angel — constitutes shirk (associating partners with Allah), which is the greatest sin.

Allah says: 'And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him' (17:23). The Quran repeatedly uses the phrase 'la ilaha illallah' — there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah — precisely because tawhid al-uluhiyyah is the essential message.

## 3. Tawhid al-Asma' wa al-Sifat — Oneness in Names and Attributes

This category affirms that Allah's names and attributes are uniquely His, without any analogy to creation. The Athari methodology — the approach of the Salaf (first three generations) — is to affirm whatever Allah has affirmed for Himself in the Quran and whatever the Prophet (peace be upon him) affirmed in authentic hadith, without distorting the meanings (tahreef), denying them (ta'til), asking how they are (takyeef), or likening them to creation (tamtheel).

Allah says: 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing' (42:11). This verse combines both negation (nothing is like Him) and affirmation (He hears and sees) — the complete Athari methodology in a single verse.

The Ash'ari and Maturidi schools, both of which are part of Ahl us-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah, affirm tawhid al-asma' wa al-sifat but employ rational theology (kalam) in explaining certain attributes. Their positions are respected within the broader tradition.

## The Relationship Between the Three Categories

The three categories are inseparable. A person who affirms Allah's lordship and attributes but directs worship to others has not fulfilled tawhid. Tawhid al-uluhiyyah is the practical fruit of the other two: knowing that Allah alone is Lord and possesses all perfect attributes should lead naturally to worshipping Him alone.

The first pillar of Islam — the shahada ('La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur rasulullah') — encapsulates all three dimensions: 'La ilaha illallah' addresses uluhiyyah and, by implication, rububiyyah and asma' wa sifat, while 'Muhammadur rasulullah' establishes the channel through which tawhid is known and lived.

## Tawhid as the Purpose of Creation

Every act of worship, every commandment of the Sharia, and every prohibition ultimately serves tawhid. Prayer purifies the heart for Allah alone. Fasting trains the soul to prefer Allah's pleasure over bodily desire. The prohibition of images that could be venerated guards against shirk. Understanding tawhid is therefore not merely an intellectual exercise — it is the lived orientation of the Muslim's entire life.
evidence_quran: Surah adh-Dhariyat 51:56 — 'I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me'
Surah Yunus 10:31 — 'Say: Who provides for you from the sky and the earth?...'
Surah al-Isra 17:23 — 'And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him'
Surah ash-Shura 42:11 — 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing'
Surah al-Anbiya 21:25 — 'And We sent no messenger before you except that We revealed to him: there is no deity except Me, so worship Me'
evidence_hadith: Abu Dawud 1479, Tirmidhi 3372 — 'Du'a is worship' (graded sahih by al-Albani)
Bukhari 7372, Muslim 30 — The Prophet told Mu'adh ibn Jabal: 'The right of Allah upon His servants is that they worship Him alone and do not associate anything with Him'
scholar_positions: The three-category division of tawhid was systematised by Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728 AH) and his student Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751 AH), and is the standard Athari presentation. Ash'ari scholars approach tawhid al-asma' wa al-sifat through the lens of rational theology (kalam), affirming Allah's oneness while interpreting certain attributes; this is an accepted position within Ahl us-Sunnah. Maturidi scholars similarly engage kalam methodology. Both schools fully agree on the core: Allah is absolutely one, without partner or equal.
sources: Ibn Taymiyyah, Majmu' al-Fatawa, vol. 1 (creed sections)
Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim (commentary on 51:56)
